en.title: Maximum Common Length of a Subsequence of X and a Substring of Y
en.description:
Find a string that is a subsequence of X and also a contiguous substring of Y, and return its maximum length. Characters of X may be skipped, but characters of Y may not; when there is no common character, output 0.

The ranges added by this site for missing bounds and the recovery of source typos are described in the input protocol.
en.input: The input is a JSON array [X,Y]. The original gives no numeric or character domain; this site adds that each string has 0..1000 Unicode scalar values, and empty strings, whitespace, control characters, and non-BMP characters are allowed; lone surrogates are not included. The total UTF-8-encoded JSON input is ≤25000 bytes.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 3; 7; 0. They have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: dp[j] stores the longest contiguous string ending at the j-th character of Y that can be a subsequence of the processed prefix of X. For each character of X read, update the matching positions in decreasing order of j to max(old value, dp[j−1]+1).
